entries.name: EN 16931-1 Electronic invoicing — Part 1: Semantic data model of the core elements of an electronic invoice
entries.versionBasis: European Commission Digital newsroom item 930407 (30/03/2026), read live: the new CEN reference is EN 16931-1:2026, and the Definitive Text was made available 18 March 2026. It replaces EN 16931-1:2017+A1:2019. CEN's own catalogue page returned HTTP 500.

licence.text: CEN/CENELEC copyright; sold via national standards bodies
licence.basis: Read cencenelec.eu/european-standardization/ipr-and-patents/copyright live today: CEN and CENELEC standards are protected by copyright, and copying (even partial), translating or distributing them without the national member's rights is illegal.

norn.overlap: invoice semantic model (BT/BG business terms), VAT breakdown, seller/buyer, lines

priority.reason: The EU semantic invoice model.

entries.notes: The 2026 edition is not backward compatible; the specification identifier is reported as urn:cen.eu:en16931:2026, but that was not checked on a primary source. The Commission funds free national access to the 2017 edition in some countries, which was not checked. Business-term IDs (BT-x) can be used as mapping vocabulary.

entries.name: OASIS UBL 2.1 Invoice schema and dependency closure
entries.versionBasis: Fetched schema header identifies UBL 2.1 OS and Release Date 04 November 2013.

licence.text: OASIS specification copyright licence / IPR policy
licence.basis: Embedded notice permits copies and implementation/explanatory derivatives with notices. Original document modifications are restricted except specified OASIS/translation cases; not an Apache grant for the standard artifact.

norn.overlap: Invoice document representation; preserve optionality, code references and precision rather than promoting source names.

priority.reason: UBL is the base of EN 16931, Peppol and several national CTC schemes.

entries.notes: Peppol's UBL 2.1 use does not mean the latest UBL release is the right syntax for every jurisdiction. Invoice is an entry point, not proof all UBL documents have been acquired. Redistribution: license-conditions. The UBL 2.3 Invoice pack (registry/packs/ubl) maps the same Invoice model through the generic XSD reader; this release still needs its own pinned read.

licence.text: OASIS specification copyright licence / IPR policy
licence.basis: Appendix K permits specification copies and implementation/explanatory derivatives with copyright and notice; document modification is restricted. Embedded third-party component/code-list terms still require review.

norn.overlap: External business-document shapes, not a promotion of UBL's entire business-object model to Core.

priority.reason: UBL is the base of EN 16931, Peppol and several national CTC schemes.

entries.notes: Profile-required UBL 2.1 is separately catalogued; current broad UBL coverage uses 2.5. Never transfer a GitHub build-tool licence to the normative standard distribution. licence.basis: Read the notice verbatim in the header of an official UN/CEFACT D16B schema file (UNECE_ActionCode_D16A.xsd), as distributed in the European Commission's EN 16931 validation repo on GitHub; unece.org returned 403. The generic UN website terms (Wayback capture) restrict site materials to personal, non-commercial use.
